scenario: AITA for getting mad at my bf for always walking in front of me? | Everytime my boyfriend and I are walking somewhere, he tends to walk much faster than me. I’m actually a pretty fast walker myself when alone, but when going out with him, either I’m in heels half the time so it’s harder to walk super fast, or even in flats, sometimes I just want to walk alongside him and hold hands and have a conversation. It’s hard to hear him or I’m struggling to keep up. I’ve brought it up to him multiple times but he says he just has longer strides (he’s maybe 6” taller than me) and can’t help it. We just went on vacation and walking around a new city, it was the same thing and I finally blew up at him saying that I don’t feel like his girlfriend when he won’t ever walk beside me. AITA and he really can’t help it?

I’m actually a pretty fast walker myself when alone, but when going out with him, either I’m in heels half the time so it’s harder to walk super fast, or even in flats, sometimes I just want to walk alongside him and hold hands and have a conversation. prediction.raw:
Answer: 1
Excuse: Your frustration is understandable, and the issue stems from a mismatch in walking styles and communication rather than a deliberate act of disrespect. While his physical differences (height, stride length) contribute to the problem, the core issue is that he hasn’t accommodated your preference for walking side-by-side—something that can be adjusted with effort (e.g., slowing down, walking beside you occasionally). Your anger was a justified response to feeling unheard and undervalued in a shared activity. The key is whether he’s willing to make *some* effort to meet you halfway (e.g., alternating sides, pausing occasionally), not whether he can "help it." If he dismisses your feelings repeatedly, that’s the real moral failing—not your frustration.
